reason: Five rapid nexts in 85 ms against 600-900 ms in FastStone is not a few tens of milliseconds, I would feel that, and I flip through folders all day. It is free and portable, so trying it costs me ten minutes.
why_switch_or_not: The speed numbers are the whole reason: next/back at 40-50 ms and a 120-350 ms open from an Explorer double-click would beat what I get in FastStone. It also has a gallery, an editor and a Space-bar preview, so I would not lose the browser and simple-editor part of FastStone. I would stay cautious because it is a one-person 0.4.1 and the benchmark is the developer's own, on one PC.
current_app_pros: FastStone's full-screen mode, its folder browser and its quick editor all work and I know every shortcut. It opens most of the formats I meet, and it has been stable for years.
current_app_pains: Fast next/next/next through a big folder lags and stutters, and the 600-900 ms for five quick nexts is exactly what I notice. It also feels old, with a dated UI and slow cold starts on big files.
objection: The numbers come from the developer's own benchmark on one PC, so I do not believe them until I time them on my machine. A single-developer 0.4.1 might also crash or have odd bugs on a file that matters, and the plug-in-free design means I cannot patch around problems.
would_change_my_mind: If it did not feel clearly faster than FastStone on my own folders and PC, or if it crashed or mangled a file in the first week, I would drop it and go back.
